case.label: D
case.text: Strongest case for D: Shield Advanced adds automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation for CloudFront and the load balancer, and covers the load balancer if attackers bypass CloudFront, which a web ACL on the distribution alone does not. It still fails, because the stem asks for the MOST cost-effective steps and a WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule plus the IP reputation managed rule group handles a GET flood from known bot addresses without a Shield Advanced subscription. C and E fail on the layer: behind CloudFront the VPC sees CloudFront addresses, not the flooding client addresses, and neither service attaches to CloudFront. Possible weaknesses, not strong enough to flag: the phrase 'already associated with bots' echoes the description of the Amazon IP reputation list and points straight to A (a wording cue); and a flood spread over many addresses could stay under a per-IP rate limit, but together A and B are still clearly the best pair.
